name: California State Senator

budget.basis: 2026-27 · Total state budget, all funds ($251.5B General Fund), in the Budget Act of 2026, which the Legislature (Senate and Assembly together) passed and the Governor signed June 29, 2026

connections.text: Elected from 40 districts to 4-year terms; even-numbered districts vote in gubernatorial election years, odd-numbered in presidential election years

citations.locator: 'June 2, 2026, Primary Election' office list, which also lists 'Governor and Lieutenant Governor'

constituents.basis: Citizens Redistricting Commission ideal Senate district population: 2020 redistricting total of 39,523,437 (Census count with 14,786 federal prisoners removed) divided by 40 districts.

citations.locator: QUALIFICATIONS: the cite printed under the 12-year term-limit requirement for State Senator and Member of the Assembly
QUALIFICATIONS: the cite printed under 'Be a U.S. citizen.'

powers.value: Senators introduce and vote on state laws and on the annual budget bill. The Legislature must pass the budget bill by June 15 and can do so by majority vote (Proposition 25, 2010); tax increases still need a two-thirds vote.

term_limit.value: 12 years total in the Legislature, in any combination of Senate and Assembly terms (Proposition 28, 2012), for members first elected after June 7, 2011. The earlier Proposition 140 (1990) limit was 8 years in the Senate and 6 in the Assembly.

notes: The budget figure is the whole state budget, because the Legislature as a body adopts it. Leadership pay effective Dec. 1, 2025: Senate President pro Tem and Minority Floor Leader $154,896; Majority Floor Leader and second-ranking Minority Leader $144,796. CONFLICT: one search summary of the CalHR page also showed an 'All Other Legislators $95,291' line, which matches the 2013-14 base pay and is probably a historical row; confirm on CalHR. A California Globe tag page (dated July 31, 2026) reports that the Commission approved 4.2% raises for 2026, which would likely take effect in December 2026; unverified. Budget conflict: one news report gives a $251.1B General Fund. The term-length figure (Senate 4 years, Assembly 2) came from a search summary that credited a 2024 commentary rather than the LAO page; verify against Cal. Const. art. IV, sec. 2(a). graph.civlab.org is reachable (2026-11-03), but CivLab maps only San Francisco and the U.S. federal government (/ca returns 404), so it has no data for this office. CONNECTIONS (primary-source batch, 2026-11-03): the verbatim quotes come from www.sos.ca.gov pages; everything from the Senate's own sites and leginfo was seen only in search summaries (www.senate.ca.gov is refused by this session's proxy, and leginfo is behind a Cloudflare challenge). Appointments are not counted, because the Senate's list of state boards with Senate appointments (3.14.25) could not be opened; the 17 Senators named in one 2025 round of appointments is not a seat count. No vote threshold for ordinary confirmations was found; Gov. Code section 1774 sets a 365-day limit (search summary). The budget-bill vote is under powers. TERM-LIMIT CONFLICT: term_limit says 'first elected after June 7, 2011', but the SOS 2014 qualifications page (opened) says 'first elected to the Legislature after June 2012'; resolve against Cal. Const. art. IV, sec. 2(a)(4). SALARY: the same SOS 2014 page gives a $952.91 State Senator filing fee (1% of the first year's salary), consistent with $95,291 being the 2013-14 pay.
